en: I can introduce myself: my name, where I am from and where I live.
I can greet people, ask how they are and say goodbye.
I can place a simple order and ask the price in a café, a bakery or a shop.
I can say numbers, the time, the date and my phone number.
I can describe my job, my family and my hobbies in a few sentences.
I can answer simple questions if people speak slowly and clearly, and ask them to repeat when I do not understand.
I can understand greetings, introductions and simple instructions said slowly and clearly.
I can understand numbers, prices and times when I hear them.
I can catch what a short answerphone message is about (who, when).
I can understand simple sentences said to me in a shop or a café.
I can understand the name, origin and job of somebody introducing themselves.
I can read and understand signs, menus and simple notices.
I can understand a short message or postcard (a greeting, an invitation, a thank you).
I can read a simple form (name, address, date of birth) and understand what is being asked for.
I can find the basic facts in a short, simple description of a person or a product.
I can find the time and the place in a programme or a timetable.
I can fill in a form with my personal details.
I can write a short greeting, thank you or invitation message.
I can write 3–5 sentences introducing myself.
I can build simple main clauses and join them with 'und' and 'aber'.
I can write about my daily routine in simple sentences.
I can use the article of a noun (der/die/das) and its plural correctly.
I can conjugate verbs in the Präsens for the subject (ich/du/er…).
I can put the verb in second place in a main clause and build a question.
I can use sein, haben and the basic modal verbs (können, möchten).
I can choose the personal and possessive pronouns correctly (ich/mein, du/dein…).
I can place separable verbs (aufstehen, anrufen) correctly in a main clause.
I can make an appointment on the phone and agree a day and a time.
I can give directions and follow directions I am given.
I can tell what I did in the past (yesterday, at the weekend, on holiday) with the Perfekt.
I can tell the doctor what is wrong and ask for medicine at the pharmacy.
I can talk about size, colour and price when shopping and ask to return something.
I can answer an invitation, make a suggestion and accept or refuse one.
I can explain a simple problem (a broken appliance, noise) politely.
I can understand the platform, the time and the delay in train and bus announcements.
I can understand the main points of a phone call about an appointment or an order.
I can follow the subject of a slow conversation and what the people want.
I can get the weather, the traffic or an event from a short radio or podcast item.
I can understand simple instructions given to me by a doctor, an official or a shop assistant.
I can understand the request, the date and the place in a short email or message.
I can pick the advert that suits me (a flat, a job, something second-hand).
I can understand a simple notice or information text (rules, opening hours).
I can understand what a short newspaper report is about.
I can follow the steps in a recipe or a set of instructions.
I can write a message suggesting a meeting to a friend with a place and a time.
I can write a short email accepting or refusing an invitation.
I can describe my holiday or my weekend in 5–8 sentences with the Perfekt.
I can write a short note of complaint or apology.
I can write sentences of reason and condition with weil, dass and wenn.
I can build the Perfekt (haben/sein + Partizip II) with regular and common irregular verbs.
I can choose the Akkusativ and Dativ articles and prepositions correctly (mit, für, zu…).
I can put the verb last in weil/dass/wenn clauses.
I can use the modal verbs (müssen, dürfen, sollen, wollen) in the Präsens and the Präteritum.
I can build the imperative (du/ihr/Sie).
I can make comparisons (größer als, am besten).
I can give my view on a subject and back it with two or three reasons.
I can tell the outline of a film, a book or an event.
I can explain what I need at an official body (the council, a bank) and get the information I want.
I can put a complaint politely but clearly and suggest a solution.
I can talk about my plans and my dreams (würde, möchte, wenn).
I can take the floor in a conversation and say whether I agree with the other person.
I can give a short two-minute presentation (myself, my town, my job).
I can understand the main idea and most of the detail in a conversation at everyday speed.
I can understand the main headlines of a news bulletin.
I can follow a person's view and their reasons in an interview.
I can understand the instructions and decisions in a meeting at work.
I can work out from a voice message what is wanted and when it is to be done.
I can understand the writer's view in a column or a forum comment.
I can understand the request and the deadline in a formal letter or email.
I can pick out the points that matter to me from an information text (health, insurance, rent).
